# Design of the R-package {.unnumbered}

name of the package: `soilharmony`

development approach (checklist)

translation of the StAP into design principles of the R package

interactions between the R-package and the WP6 database

long-term hosting and maintenance (CRAN)

Rough ideas for end-user functions:

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

# install latest development version from soilharmony github organization
pak::pkg_install("soilharmony/soilharmony")

library(soilharmony)


# test for method equivalence
soilharmony::sh_equivalence(
  y1 = ph_iso_bla_bla,
  y2 = ph_local_protocol,
  relative_diff = FALSE,
  delta = ringtest_ph,
  data = large_european_dataset
)

# calibrate a new TF
soilharmony::sh_calibrate(
  formula = ph_refmethod ~ ph_nonrefmethod * soil_unit,
  data = large_european_dataset
)

# validate a TF against new data
soilharmony::sh_validate(
  tf_id = "unique_id_for_the_TF_in_the_WP6_database",
  validation_data = soilharmony_wp4_dataset_4000samples
)

# end-user makes predictions (function should be called by the RShiny app)
soilharmony::sh_predict(
  tf_id = "unique_id_for_the_TF_in_the_WP6_database",
  new_observations = my_new_measurements_in_2028
)
```
